subject: science

sections.scope_note: Arizona standards deferred per Ivan (2026-10-03). This crosswalk covers Florida NGSSS Science ↔ IB PYP Science only.

rows.key_differences: Florida specifies systematic investigation, comparing group observations, and evidence-based reasoning. PYP develops inquiry skills across transdisciplinary contexts.
rows.suggested_instructional_bridge: Conduct collaborative investigations where students compare methods and results across groups, emphasizing evidence-based conclusions.

rows.topic_domain: Nature of Science - Recording and Explaining
rows.key_differences: Florida specifies distinguishing observations from inferences, evidence-based explanations, and creativity in science. PYP develops inquiry dispositions.
rows.suggested_instructional_bridge: Use science notebooks to record careful observations, develop creative explanations, and distinguish what was observed from what was inferred.

rows.topic_domain: Nature of Science - Focus and Models
rows.key_differences: Florida specifies science focuses on the natural world and models can take multiple forms. PYP uses models to understand phenomena.
rows.suggested_instructional_bridge: Create various types of models (physical, drawings, mental, digital) to explain natural phenomena, exploring how different forms serve different purposes.

rows.key_differences: Florida specifies physical properties, states of water, conservation of mass, and magnetism. PYP explores materials through inquiry.
rows.suggested_instructional_bridge: Investigate material properties through hands-on exploration, connecting observations to conservation of mass and magnetic properties.

rows.key_differences: Florida specifies familiar changes (decay, burning, rusting, cooking) that create different materials. PYP explores change as key concept.
rows.suggested_instructional_bridge: Investigate everyday chemical and physical changes, classifying by whether new materials are created and connecting to the concept of change.

rows.key_differences: Florida specifies light, heat, sound, electrical, and motion energy, plus sound production and wind/water energy. PYP explores energy through function concept.
rows.suggested_instructional_bridge: Investigate energy forms through experiments—vibration/sound, wind/water motion—connecting observations to energy function in the world.

rows.key_differences: Florida specifies heat flow from hot to cold and thermal conductors/insulators. PYP connects to causation in energy transfer.
rows.suggested_instructional_bridge: Design insulation experiments exploring how materials affect heat transfer, connecting cause-effect relationships to engineering applications.

rows.key_differences: Florida specifies position change, direction change, and speed calculations. PYP explores motion through change concept.
rows.suggested_instructional_bridge: Investigate motion through distance/time experiments, calculating speeds and exploring how motion changes with different forces.

rows.key_differences: Florida specifies pollination, fertilization, seed production, dispersal, and germination. PYP explores plant function through inquiry.
rows.suggested_instructional_bridge: Grow plants from seed, observing and documenting the full reproduction cycle, connecting each stage to its function in plant survival.

rows.key_differences: Florida specifies inherited vs. environmental traits and sexual reproduction in animals. PYP connects inheritance to organism-environment relationships.
rows.suggested_instructional_bridge: Compare traits in families and species, exploring what is inherited versus what is shaped by environment, connecting to diversity in populations.

rows.key_differences: Florida specifies comparing Florida plant/animal life cycles including metamorphosis types. PYP explores life cycles through change concept.
rows.suggested_instructional_bridge: Compare life cycles of local Florida organisms, investigating complete versus incomplete metamorphosis and flowering versus non-flowering plants.

ib_framework_elements: PYP Transdisciplinary Theme: Sharing the planet
rows.key_differences: Florida specifies seasonal changes, energy in food chains, producers/consumers/decomposers, and ecosystem changes. PYP addresses through 'Sharing the planet'.
rows.suggested_instructional_bridge: Study Florida ecosystems—seasonal changes, food webs, invasive species impacts—connecting to 'Sharing the planet' responsibility themes.

rows.key_differences: Florida specifies star patterns, moon phases, Earth's rotation/revolution, and day/night connections. PYP explores space through observable patterns and change.
rows.suggested_instructional_bridge: Track moon phases and star patterns over time, connecting observations to Earth's rotation and revolution cycles.

ib_framework_elements: PYP Transdisciplinary Theme: How we organize ourselves
rows.key_differences: Florida specifically addresses space program effects on Florida's economy and culture. PYP addresses human systems more broadly.
rows.suggested_instructional_bridge: Investigate Kennedy Space Center's role in Florida, connecting space exploration to economic and cultural impacts within 'How we organize ourselves'.

rows.key_differences: Florida specifies three rock categories and mineral physical properties. PYP explores Earth materials through form concept.
rows.suggested_instructional_bridge: Collect and classify rocks and minerals, identifying properties and categorizing by formation process, connecting to rock cycle understanding.

ib_framework_elements: PYP Transdisciplinary Theme: Sharing the planet
rows.key_differences: Florida specifies renewable/nonrenewable resources, weathering/erosion, technology for observation, and Florida resources. PYP addresses through resource responsibility.
rows.suggested_instructional_bridge: Investigate Florida's resources (phosphate, solar, water) and weathering/erosion, connecting to 'Sharing the planet' sustainability themes.
